t.pt: แล้วหรือยัง: o 'já?' do tailandês
t.en: แล้วหรือยัง: asking 'already?'

e.pt: O แล้ว avisa que a coisa já aconteceu ou que o estado já vale: มีแล้วครับ é 'já tenho'. Na pergunta ele vem amarrado ao หรือยัง — คุณมีครอบครัวแล้วหรือยังครับ ('você já tem família?') — e a resposta ecoa o แล้ว: มีแล้วครับ. É o nosso 'já...?' de 'você já almoçou?', só que aqui o แล้ว é obrigatório para dizer que a bola já está em jogo. Sem ele, คุณมีครอบครัวครับ pergunta apenas se a pessoa tem família, sem nenhuma ideia de 'até agora'.
e.en: แล้ว marks that something has happened or now holds: มีแล้วครับ 'I already have (one)'. In questions it comes with หรือยัง (คุณมีครอบครัวแล้วหรือยังครับ), and the answer echoes the แล้ว (มีแล้วครับ). Without it the question is a plain 'do you have a family?', with no 'by now' sense.

notas.ex: คุณ|kun มี|mii ครอบครัว|krɔ̂ɔp-kruua แล้ว|lɛ́ɛo หรือยัง|rʉ̌ʉ-yang ครับ|kráp

t.pt: ยังไม่เคย...เลย: o 'nunca' com prazo de validade
t.en: ยังไม่เคย...เลย: 'never (so far)'

e.pt: เคย diz que a pessoa já experimentou aquilo alguma vez na vida. Negando com ยังไม่ e fechando a frase com เลย, você obtém o 'nunca... até agora': ผมยังไม่เคยไปสำนักงานยูซิสเลย ('nunca fui ao escritório da USIS'). O เลย do fim é o que dá o gosto de 'nem uma vez sequer'; sem ele a frase continua correta, só menos enfática. Repare que o tailandês não tem um verbo para 'nunca': ele empilha negação + เคย + เลย, do jeito que a gente empilha 'nunca... na vida'.
e.en: เคย says you have experienced something before. Negated as ยังไม่เคย and closed off with เลย it gives 'never... so far': ผมยังไม่เคยไปสำนักงานยูซิสเลย 'I've never been to the USIS office'. The final เลย adds 'not even once'; without it the sentence is still correct, only less emphatic.

t.pt: มา + verbo: o que você veio fazer
t.en: มา + verb: what you came to do

e.pt: O มา ('vir') gruda direto no verbo que explica o motivo da vinda, sem preposição nenhuma no meio: มาทำงาน ('vim trabalhar'), มาเรียน ('vim estudar'). Na pergunta, o verbo vira อะไร — คุณมาทำอะไรที่นี่ครับ ('o que você veio fazer aqui?') — e a resposta devolve o mesmo molde: ผมมาทำงานที่ยูซิสครับ, com o ที่ puxando o lugar. É o nosso 'vim fazer o quê?', na ordem vir + fazer + onde. O mesmo vale para o ไป: ไปธุระ é 'sair para resolver um assunto'.
e.en: มา 'come' is glued straight onto the verb that states the purpose, with no preposition: มาทำงาน 'come to work', มาเรียน 'come to study'. In the question the verb becomes อะไร (คุณมาทำอะไรที่นี่ครับ) and the answer repeats the frame (ผมมาทำงานที่ยูซิสครับ), with ที่ introducing the place. The same holds for ไป (ไปธุระ).

notas.ex: คุณ|kun มา|maa ทำ|tam อะไร|à-rai ที่นี่|tîi-nîi ครับ|kráp

t.pt: ลา só sai da boca de quem vai embora
t.en: ลา is said only by the person leaving

e.pt: O livro é explícito no vocabulário: ลา ('dizer tchau') é palavra de quem parte — quem fica não usa. No diálogo o Maen fecha a conversa em três passos: dá o motivo (จะรีบไปธุระ, 'preciso correr para resolver um assunto'), avisa que está saindo (ผมลาก่อนนะครับ) e o Tom responde só ครับ. Aí vem o fecho de cortesia de quem fica: หวังว่าเราคงได้พบกันอีก ('espero que a gente se encontre de novo'). É o nosso 'já vou indo, tá?', com uma diferença de etiqueta: em tailandês dizer o motivo faz parte da despedida educada, não soa a justificativa.
e.en: The vocabulary is explicit: ลา 'to say goodbye' is used only by the person leaving. In the dialog Maen gives the reason (จะรีบไปธุระ), announces the departure (ผมลาก่อนนะครับ) and Tom simply answers ครับ; the one who stays adds a courteous closing, หวังว่าเราคงได้พบกันอีก 'I hope we'll meet again'. Stating the reason is part of polite leavetaking, not an excuse.

notas.ex: ผม|pǒm ลา|laa ก่อน|gɔ̀ɔn นะ|ná ครับ|kráp
